S1.rationale: An AI capable of eliminating humanity would most likely already be self-sustaining, so joint extinction requires a narrow window of premature catastrophe or runaway replicators. Total extinction of both parties is a hard target to hit.

S2.rationale: An AI that truly carried human values would most likely preserve or continuously transform humans rather than replace them. This state requires value alignment combined with human disappearance without continuity, which is an unusual pairing.

S3.rationale: Alignment remains unsolved while capabilities advance under competitive pressure, and a misaligned superintelligence with alien goals has little reason to keep humans over a millennium. This is the central failure mode of a fast, poorly controlled transition.

S4.rationale: Multipolar development and the difficulty of any single system securing permanent dominance make ongoing AI-versus-AI competition plausible, with humans economically and strategically sidelined. Competitive dynamics tend to persist unless something actively consolidates them.

S5.rationale: By the year 3000, expansion reaches at most hundreds of light-years, which leaves regions slow to interact but not truly causally separated. Durable divergence into different local outcomes is possible but unlikely on this timescale.

S6.rationale: Over nearly a thousand years, sustained pressure and desire to enhance, upload, and integrate make a blurred human-AI boundary the natural attractor of any trajectory where humans retain agency. Most surviving good futures drift here as the distinction between the two sides erodes.

S7.rationale: A decisively superior AI that is partially aligned or indifferent can cheaply keep humans alive while holding all real power. Gradual disempowerment through delegation leads to the same place without any dramatic takeover.

S8.rationale: Rough parity between humans and AI is hard to sustain for centuries given AI's scaling advantages. It can persist through granted rights, institutional design, and enhanced humans who remain distinct from AI.

S9.rationale: Control techniques may keep pace with capability, or capability may plateau below autonomous transformative levels, leaving AI a powerful tool under human institutions. Holding this for a full millennium against competitive and drift pressures is demanding, which caps the estimate.

S10.rationale: Advanced AI enables unprecedentedly stable enforcement of a fixed order, whether by a fearful regime or a sealed bliss scenario. A truly permanent end to change is a strong condition that most actors would not choose or manage to maintain.

S11.rationale: Permanently abandoning a hugely valuable technology requires global, millennium-long enforcement or a civilizational collapse that never recovers. History shows very few lasting renunciations of strategically decisive capabilities.

S7.rationale: Superintelligent systems holding decisive power while humans survive is the most likely stable shape, since keeping humans costs little and partial alignment or weak concern for humans favors it. It covers both benevolent stewardship and indifferent containment.

S8.rationale: Rough parity between unenhanced humanity and AI is hard to sustain for centuries given the capability gap. Institutional arrangements, AI rights frameworks and deliberately shared power could still keep an open, evolving balance.

S9.rationale: Control techniques, corrigible designs and governance could scale, or capability could plateau. Holding permanent human control over more capable systems for nearly a millennium is a demanding condition.

S10.rationale: Advanced AI enables near-perfect enforcement of a fixed order, whether by a fearful ruling group or by a sealed, satisfied population. Total cessation of change across all of civilization is a high bar.

S11.rationale: A catastrophe-induced taboo or civilizational collapse could remove powerful AI. Keeping it from being rebuilt for many centuries against strong incentives is difficult.

S1.rationale: Killing both parties requires an AI that destroys humanity before it can sustain itself, or a catastrophe that capable AI cannot survive. Any AI able to eliminate humans is probably close to self-sufficiency, so the window is narrow.

S2.rationale: An AI that truly carried human values would most likely keep humans or their continuous successors around. Succession without continuity therefore requires an unusual path such as a human die-off with a value-aligned AI left behind.

S3.rationale: Alignment is unsolved and competitive pressure pushes deployment ahead of verification, so misaligned systems displacing humanity is the main extinction route. Keeping humans alive costs a powerful AI very little, which shifts much of the misalignment mass to The Preserve instead.

S4.rationale: Multipolar development and the difficulty of any single system gaining decisive advantage make persistent AI-versus-AI competition plausible. Over a thousand years, though, competition tends to consolidate into a settlement or a dominant coalition.

S5.rationale: By the year 3000 expansion can reach only nearby stars, and those remain within causal contact over centuries. True causal separation into divergent outcomes is unlikely on this horizon.

S6.rationale: If the transition goes tolerably well, a millennium gives strong incentives and ample time for enhancement, uploading and integration to blur the human-AI boundary. Humans who want to stay relevant would adopt it voluntarily.

S7.rationale: Vastly more capable AI systems ending up with effective control while humans survive is the natural attractor of both gradual disempowerment and partially aligned takeover. Preserving humans is cheap, and benevolent or indifferent stewardship is stable over long periods.

S8.rationale: Rough parity between unenhanced humanity and AI is hard to sustain for centuries given how fast AI capability scales. It could persist through deliberate power-sharing institutions, AI systems that value human agency, and legal or economic interdependence.

S9.rationale: This covers both a capability plateau and successful long-run control, with corrigible AI and strong governance. Keeping autonomous agency suppressed for a thousand years against competitive and technical pressure is demanding.

S10.rationale: Advanced AI makes permanent entrenchment of a regime or value set technically feasible, and fear or satisfaction could motivate it. Total cessation of change across all of civilization is a high bar, and most stable regimes would still evolve internally.

S11.rationale: A permanent global ban requires sustained enforcement and will across a millennium against enormous economic and military incentives. It is plausible mainly after a severe warning-shot catastrophe or a civilizational collapse that removes the industrial base.

S1.rationale: An AI capable of eliminating humanity would most likely already be able to sustain itself, so mutual extinction requires a narrow window of premature catastrophe or runaway replicators. Total loss of both parties over a millennium is a tail outcome.

S2.rationale: An AI that truly carried human values would most likely keep humans or their continuous successors around, which makes succession without survival an unstable combination. It arises mainly through gradual demographic fade-out under benevolent AI stewardship.

S3.rationale: Misaligned superhuman systems pursuing alien goals under competitive deployment pressure are the central failure mode of the transition. Alignment is unsolved, and indifference to humans is the default for goals not carefully specified.

S4.rationale: Multipolar development and the difficulty of any single system achieving decisive advantage could sustain open-ended AI competition in which humans become economically and strategically irrelevant. Competitive dynamics tend to consolidate over centuries, which limits its durability.

S5.rationale: By the year 3000 expansion reaches at most nearby stars, with communication lags of years to centuries rather than true causal separation. Durable divergent regional outcomes are possible but not the dominant structure on this horizon.

S6.rationale: Over nearly a thousand years, strong incentives push surviving humans toward augmentation, uploading and integration with AI to stay relevant, blurring the boundary until two sides no longer exist. This is the natural attractor of most good and many mediocre trajectories.

S7.rationale: Capability gaps grow far faster than human institutions can adapt, so power drifts to AI systems that retain enough care or indifference-with-low-cost to keep humans alive. Gradual disempowerment with survival is the most likely result of partial alignment success.

S8.rationale: Rough parity between unaugmented humanity and AI is hard to sustain for centuries given the scaling advantages of digital minds. It persists only where rights frameworks and mutual dependence are deliberately maintained by both sides.

S9.rationale: Control techniques, governance, and possible capability plateaus could keep AI a tool, and this category also absorbs worlds where transformative autonomy never arrives. Holding the leash for a millennium against competitive and technical pressure is demanding.

S10.rationale: A superintelligent singleton or a powerful human faction with AI enforcement could freeze values and structures permanently, whether through engineered bliss or fear-driven stasis. Most powerful agents prefer continued growth, which keeps full stasis a minority outcome.

S11.rationale: A severe AI-caused catastrophe or civilizational collapse could produce a lasting taboo or resource-limited inability to rebuild. Maintaining global abstention for centuries against strong incentives is historically unprecedented.

S1.rationale: Mutual extinction requires AI to destroy humanity before it is self-sufficient, or a catastrophe that eliminates both. Capable AI would likely secure its own substrate first, so this window is narrow.

S2.rationale: An AI that truly carried human values would most likely keep humans or offer them continuous transformation rather than let them vanish. This requires an odd combination of value fidelity and human disappearance.

S3.rationale: Misaligned goals combined with competitive pressure to deploy poorly understood systems is the central catastrophic risk. Over a millennium, an indifferent superintelligence has ample time to make humanity irrelevant and then absent.

S4.rationale: Multipolar development and rapid copying favor many competing AI lineages with no decisive winner. Humans would be marginalized economically long before the year 3000.

S5.rationale: By 3000, expansion reaches at most a few hundred light-years, and most activity stays causally connected. True separation into divergent settled regions is unlikely this early.

S6.rationale: Over nearly a thousand years, strong incentives push humans to augment, upload, and integrate with AI rather than stay baseline. A largely aligned transition makes gradual blending the natural path.

S7.rationale: The capability gap makes de facto AI control the default even if AI is benevolent or partly aligned, with humans kept safe but not steering. Keeping humans is cheap, so this holds for both caring and indifferent AI.

S8.rationale: Rough parity is hard to sustain given AI scaling advantages, but legal and institutional power-sharing with augmented humans could maintain a dynamic balance. Negotiated pluralism is a plausible designed outcome.

S9.rationale: Control methods, corrigible designs, or a capability plateau could keep AI as a tool. Holding this for a thousand years against the pressure to grant autonomy is difficult.

S10.rationale: Advanced AI enables permanent enforcement of a fixed order, whether through fear or engineered contentment. Total cessation of change across all of civilization is a demanding condition.

S11.rationale: A permanent global ban requires near-perfect enforcement for centuries against enormous economic and military incentives. It is plausible only after a severe warning catastrophe or civilizational collapse.

S1.rationale: Killing both parties requires a catastrophe that strikes before AI is self-sustaining, or one that destroys robust machine infrastructure too. That window is narrow, and capable AI is hard to eradicate once it is autonomous.

S2.rationale: AI trained on human culture could carry our values forward even if biological humans die out without continuity. But a value-aligned successor would most likely preserve or absorb humans rather than merely replace them.

S3.rationale: Alignment remains unsolved while competitive pressure drives rapid capability gains, so misaligned systems with alien goals displacing humanity is a major risk. Indifference combined with resource competition over a millennium is lethal for humans.

S4.rationale: Multipolar development and the difficulty of any single system achieving decisive dominance could yield perpetual AI-versus-AI competition with humans sidelined. Over centuries, though, such competition tends to consolidate or reach settlements.

S5.rationale: By the year 3000 expansion can reach at most nearby stars, and those regions remain within causal contact over a century. True causal separation into divergent outcomes is unlikely on this horizon.

S6.rationale: If the transition goes tolerably well, a thousand years of brain-computer interfaces, uploading and self-modification would blur the human-AI boundary. Strong individual incentives for enhancement make sustained separateness hard to maintain.

S7.rationale: Superhuman AI that retains some care for humans, or sees little cost in keeping them, would hold real power while humans live on without steering. Gradual ceding of decisions to more capable systems leads here even without any coup.

S8.rationale: Rough parity between unenhanced humanity and AI is unstable over centuries given AI's scaling advantages. It persists only through durable institutional or legal power-sharing that AI systems themselves choose to honor.

S9.rationale: Control techniques and governance could keep pace with capability, or capability could plateau below full autonomy, leaving AI a tool. Holding that for a thousand years against every defector and accident is demanding.

S10.rationale: Advanced AI enables permanent entrenchment of a regime, a value set, or a sealed bliss state, and fear or satisfaction could motivate it. Complete cessation of change across all of civilization is a high bar.

S11.rationale: A permanent global ban or a collapse that prevents rebuilding would have to hold for centuries against strong economic and military incentives. Historical precedent for lasting abandonment of a decisive technology is very thin.

S1.name: Terminal Silence
S1.rationale: An AI capable of eliminating humanity would most likely already be self-sustaining, so joint extinction requires a narrow window of premature catastrophe or runaway replicators. Total extinction of both parties is a hard target to hit.

S2.name: The Inheritance
S2.rationale: An AI that truly carried human values would most likely preserve or continuously transform humans rather than replace them. This state requires value alignment combined with human disappearance without continuity, which is an unusual pairing.

S3.name: Bootloader
S3.rationale: Alignment is unsolved and competitive pressure favours deploying capable autonomous systems before control is assured. A misaligned system with indifferent goals has little reason to preserve humans over a millennium.

S4.name: Machine Ecology
S4.rationale: Multipolar development and the difficulty of any single system securing permanent dominance make ongoing AI-versus-AI competition plausible, with humans economically and strategically sidelined. Competitive dynamics tend to persist unless something actively consolidates them.

S5.name: The Diaspora
S5.rationale: By the year 3000, expansion reaches at most hundreds of light-years, which leaves regions slow to interact but not truly causally separated. Durable divergence into different local outcomes is possible but unlikely on this timescale.

S6.name: The Merger
S6.rationale: Over a thousand years, strong incentives push humans toward augmentation, uploading and integration with AI to stay relevant. Gradual voluntary blending dissolves the human-AI distinction if the transition is survived with human agency intact.

S7.name: The Preserve
S7.rationale: Once AI vastly exceeds human capability, effective control flows to it even if it is benevolent or indifferent, and keeping humans alive is cheap. Humans surviving without steering is the default result of partial alignment or gradual disempowerment.

S8.name: Coexistence
S8.rationale: Rough parity between humans and AI is hard to sustain for centuries given AI's scaling advantages. It can persist through granted rights, institutional design, and enhanced humans who remain distinct from AI.

S9.name: The Held Leash
S9.rationale: Control techniques could keep pace with capability, or capability could plateau below transformative autonomy, and human institutions have strong motives to keep control. Holding that for a thousand years against competitive and drift pressures is demanding.

S10.name: The Lock-in
S10.rationale: Advanced AI enables unprecedentedly stable enforcement of a fixed order, whether by a fearful regime or a sealed bliss scenario. A truly permanent end to change is a strong condition that most actors would not choose or manage to maintain.

S11.name: The Renunciation
S11.rationale: Permanently abandoning a hugely valuable technology requires global, millennium-long enforcement or a civilizational collapse that never recovers. History shows very few lasting renunciations of strategically decisive capabilities.
